data.instructions_html:
You will hear a short speech clip in Swahili, which may be a real recording or computer-generated, together with the text it is supposed to say. Listen to the whole clip, then answer two separate questions.

1. Naturalness is about how the voice sounds.

  • Does it sound like a real person speaking?
  • Judge only the sound, not whether the words are correct.

2. Intelligibility is about the words.

  • Listen while reading the text: are all the words clear and the same as in the text? Look out for words that are unclear, wrong, missing, added or repeated, or cut off.
  • Listen to the pronunciation: a word that is pronounced as a different word, even a similar-sounding one, is a wrong word.
  • A word you cannot make out is an error, even if you can guess it from the text.

Answer each question on its own: a natural voice can say the wrong words, and a poor voice can say the right words.

1. Naturalness is about how the voice sounds.

  • Does it sound like a real person speaking?
  • Judge only the sound, not whether the words are correct.

2. Intelligibility is about the words.

  • Listen while reading the text: are all the words clear and the same as in the text? Look out for words that are unclear, wrong, missing, added or repeated, or cut off.
  • Listen to the pronunciation: a word that is pronounced as a different word, even a similar-sounding one, is a wrong word.
  • A word you cannot make out is an error, even if you can guess it from the text.

Answer each question on its own: a natural voice can say the wrong words, and a poor voice can say the right words.

1. Naturalness is about how the voice sounds.

  • Does it sound like a real person speaking?
  • Judge only the sound, not whether the words are correct.

2. Intelligibility is about the words.

  • Listen while reading the text: are all the words clear and the same as in the text? Look out for words that are unclear, wrong, missing, added or repeated, or cut off.
  • Listen to the pronunciation: a word that is pronounced as a different word, even a similar-sounding one, is a wrong word.
  • A word you cannot make out is an error, even if you can guess it from the text.

Answer each question on its own: a natural voice can say the wrong words, and a poor voice can say the right words.
